Pinterest Marketing for Etsy Sellers: Get Found in Search

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

A common Etsy routine goes like this: save your listing photos to a board called "My Shop," paste the listing title into the pin title, and wait. Traction is usually thin. The reason is not that Pinterest is wrong for handmade or custom items. It is that Pinterest works as a visual search engine, and a bare product photo with a marketplace-style title does not answer anything a person searched for. If that distinction is new, start with Pinterest as a search engine or social media, then come back here.

Your listing title and your pin title do different jobs

The same item needs two different pieces of writing, because two different systems read them.

The listing title

This is written for the marketplace: item words, materials, style, the details a buyer scans for. It can read a little like a stack of keywords, and that is fine there.

The pin title

A pin title can run up to 100 characters, and roughly the first 40 are the ones most likely to show. Lead with the phrase a searcher would use, and write it so a person would want to click. Take a listing titled "Personalized Teacher Gift Tumbler Custom Name Cup." The pin can instead say "Teacher Appreciation Gift Ideas She Will Actually Use." Same product, but the pin now meets a search instead of repeating a tag list.

Give the description (up to 500 characters) one or two plain sentences about who the item is for and when someone would give or use it, and fill in the alt text (also up to 500 characters) to describe what is in the image. For the full method, see SEO-friendly Pinterest pin titles.

Build boards around search topics, not around your shop

A board named "Shop Favorites" tells Pinterest nothing. A board named for a topic a shopper would search does. Try boards such as:

  • Teacher appreciation gift ideas
  • Bridesmaid and wedding party gifts
  • Farmhouse kitchen decor
  • Gifts for new moms

Swap in the topics that fit your own catalog. Put the main phrase in the board title, add a short keyword-rich description, and keep every board to one clear theme so each pin has an obvious home. The board SEO guide covers titles and descriptions in detail.

Plan seasonal pins before the season

Shopping for handmade and gift items is often tied to an occasion: holidays, graduations, back to school, weddings. Pins take time to be found, so a pin published in the middle of the season may arrive late. Publish seasonal pins ahead of the occasion, and keep them live afterward, since pins can keep surfacing for months. A simple Pinterest content calendar that works backward from your busiest occasions is enough to start.

Send each pin to the most specific page

  1. Link a pin about one item to that listing, and a pin about a theme to the shop section that holds it.
  2. Add UTM tracking so your analytics shows which pins send visitors.
  3. Check links regularly, because a pin pointing at a removed listing wastes the click.
  4. Make several distinct pins for your best sellers, each aimed at a different search.

What to do this week

  1. Pick your top five listings.
  2. For each one, write down two phrases a buyer might search that are not the listing title.
  3. Rename or create boards that match those phrases.
  4. Write one new pin title and description per phrase, using the keyword first.
  5. Note the date, then review saves and clicks after a few weeks. Pinterest results build over weeks and months of consistent effort, not days.

If your shop has many similar items, read Pinterest marketing for custom product and print shops. If your work is made by hand, the handmade business guide covers process and story content. Once shoppers arrive, Pinterest SEO for Shopify stores shows how the same thinking applies to your own storefront.

Frequently asked questions

Do Etsy sellers need Pinterest if they already get traffic from the marketplace?

Pinterest is a separate search engine where people look for ideas before they decide what to buy. It can add a second discovery route to your shop, but it takes weeks or months of consistent pinning to build, so treat it as long term rather than a quick fix.

Should my pin title match my Etsy listing title?

Usually not. A listing title is written for the marketplace, while a pin title should lead with the phrase a searcher would type on Pinterest. Pin titles can be up to 100 characters, and roughly the first 40 are the most likely to show.

How many boards does an Etsy shop need on Pinterest?

Enough that every pin has a clear topic home, and no more. Start with a handful of boards named for real searches such as gift ideas or decor themes, then add boards as new topics earn their place.

When should I publish seasonal pins?

Before the occasion, not during it. Pins can take time to be found, so publish ahead of the season and leave them live afterward, since a pin can keep surfacing for months.
